result.summary: This PR changes the bitcoinkernel C API so log entries are delivered as a struct (timestamp, thread, level, category, file/line, message) instead of a pre-formatted string, and simplifies the kernel's logging configuration to a single min-level filter. It removes logging.cpp from the kernel build by giving the kernel its own KernelLogger backend implementing the util::log hooks, and drops buffering, disable, and per-category enable/disable functions that no longer make sense for a library consumer. Node (bitcoind) logging behavior is unchanged except for a developer-notes update.
result.problem: Kernel library consumers currently must parse formatted log strings to recover structured fields, and the level/category filtering interface designed for the node's many log categories is unintuitive and unnecessary overhead for a library where consumers can filter themselves. This affects anyone building against libbitcoinkernel (issue #34062, part of the kernel library project #27587).

ajtowns' concern about conditional argument evaluation for Info+ levels reverted and pinned with a unit test.
ryanofsky's suggestion to split out move-only changes was implemented via separate merged PR #34465.

result.card: This PR reworks the bitcoinkernel C logging API to deliver structured log entries (timestamp, thread, category, level, file/line) instead of formatted strings, and collapses the configuration surface down to a single min-level filter, removing buffering and per-category enable/disable machinery that made sense for the node but not for a library. It closes issue #34062 (RFC: separate kernel logging infrastructure), part of the libbitcoinkernel project (#27587), and removes logging.cpp from the kernel build entirely. Reviewer ryanofsky gave a strong concept/approach ACK calling it 'thoughtfully implemented' and says he plans to rebase his own kernel PR #30342 on top of it. The PR had a long, multi-month back-and-forth on API shape (Dispatcher design, argument-evaluation semantics) with ajtowns and purpleKarrot, all resolved through rework, and a real mutex-deadlock bug found by w0xlt was fixed in the most recent force-push (2026-09-17), leaving the PR currently in an actively reviewed, mergeable-looking state. No open unresolved objections remain.
